summary_en: Work orders, contractors, assets and preventive maintenance.
summary_fr: Interventions, prestataires, équipements et maintenance préventive.

tools.name: Advizeo
tools.positioning: Energy management that ends in a works order — engineering-led rather than reporting-led.
tools.description: Advizeo, part of the Setec engineering group, provides energy monitoring and management for French buildings: meter and building management system data collection, consumption analysis and alerting, décret tertiaire declaration support, and an action plan followed through to implementation.
tools.real_estate_use: Its difference from a pure reporting platform is the engineering behind it. Detecting that a building's heating runs at weekends is only useful if someone changes the schedule. Advizeo pairs the monitoring with technical recommendations and follow-up, which suits owners who do not have an in-house energy engineer.
features: Meter, submeter and building management system data collection
Consumption analysis with drift and anomaly alerting
Décret tertiaire declaration and OPERAT support
Technical action plans with quantified savings
Works and measure follow-up over time
Multi-site portfolio dashboards

use_cases.job: Detect and correct consumption drift instead of only reporting it
Meet décret tertiaire obligations with a costed action plan behind the declaration

tools.name: BOB Desk
tools.positioning: Maintenance and compliance tracking for multi-site French operators — retail chains, restaurants, agencies.
tools.description: BOB Desk is a French SaaS for maintenance and regulatory compliance management across multiple sites: intervention requests, provider dispatch, preventive planning, quote and invoice control, equipment records and regulatory inspection tracking.
tools.real_estate_use: A chain with two hundred outlets carries a compliance calendar per site — fire safety, electrical inspection, extraction, refrigeration — and no realistic way to track it in a spreadsheet. BOB Desk holds the obligations per site with their due dates, and routes the corrective work to the contracted provider, keeping the evidence in one place for an inspection.
features: Multi-site intervention request and dispatch
Preventive maintenance and regulatory inspection calendars
Provider contracts and performance tracking
Quote and invoice control against agreed rates
Equipment registry per site
Compliance evidence storage and reporting

use_cases.job: Track regulatory inspection deadlines across hundreds of sites
Control maintenance quotes and invoices against contracted rates

tools.name: Breezeway
tools.positioning: Property operations and guest experience platform for the teams cleaning, inspecting and servicing short-term rentals.
tools.description: Breezeway coordinates the field work behind a short-term rental portfolio rather than the booking side. It schedules cleaning and maintenance tasks, dispatches them to cleaners and vendors through a mobile app with photo checklists, tracks inventory and supplies, pays cleaners, and reports on what was done. A second product line handles guest communication: messaging, digital welcome books, an AI assistant answering guest questions, and paid upsells. A freemium tier covers a single property.
tools.real_estate_use: A vacation rental manager with a scattered portfolio and a mix of employed and subcontracted cleaners has the same problem every turnover day: knowing that each property was actually cleaned, inspected and restocked before the next guest arrives. Breezeway turns each departure into a scheduled task with a photo checklist the cleaner completes on their phone, so the manager sees evidence rather than a claim, and damage or a missing item surfaces as a work order before the guest does. Pricing is per property, which is why managers of five homes and of five hundred both use it, and residential and corporate housing operators use the same operations layer.
features: Task scheduling and work coordination across field teams
Mobile checklists with photo capture, available in several languages
Work order and preventive maintenance management
Inventory and supply tracking
Cleaner and vendor payments
Guest messaging with digital guidebooks, AI answering and paid upsells

use_cases.job: Prove every turnover was cleaned and inspected before the next check-in
Turn a defect spotted during a clean into a dispatched work order

tools.name: Condo Control
tools.positioning: Condo and HOA management software organised around the building's daily life: communication, amenities, security desk and maintenance, with accounting alongside.
tools.description: Condo Control is software for condominium and homeowner association management, sold to management companies, self-managed communities and security companies. Its modules cover communication (announcements, discussion forum, association websites, virtual meetings and an AI manager assistant), financial work (accounting, billing and collections, portfolio accounting, reports and budgeting, online payments, vendor management), maintenance (requests, architectural change, preventive maintenance, community assets), record keeping (resident database, file library, violation tracking, proxy and fractional voting, electronic consent), security (authorised entry, incident reports, key tracking, security logs and patrol, package management) and the resident side (guest passes, event calendar, amenity booking, package tracking, visitor parking). The vendor also sells managed accounting and moderated meeting services alongside the software.
tools.real_estate_use: A condominium tower runs on things a rental building never has to think about: a front desk logging visitors, a party room booked three weeks ahead, a package wall that overflows every December, a proxy count that has to hold up at the annual general meeting. Condo Control is the product that treats those as first-class, which is why concierge and security staff use it as much as the property manager. A manager reaches for it when the building's problem is coordination rather than accounting, and when the board wants residents to self-serve on bookings, documents and payments instead of calling the office. Its pricing is quoted per unit band with distinct plans for self-managed communities and for management companies.
features: Amenity booking, guest passes and visitor parking
Package tracking and package room management
Front desk security logs, patrol, incident reports and key tracking
Violation tracking and rule enforcement
Proxy and fractional voting with electronic consent
Maintenance requests, preventive maintenance and architectural change requests

use_cases.job: Run an AGM with a proxy count that holds up, without paper
Book the party room and see whether a package has arrived without calling the desk
Track a maintenance request from a resident report to a vendor visit

tools.name: Corrigo
tools.positioning: A CMMS shaped by a global services firm running it on its own managed portfolios.
tools.description: Corrigo is a facilities and work order management platform: service requests, vendor dispatch and scoring, preventive maintenance, asset lifecycle tracking and spend analytics. It is developed inside JLL and deployed both on JLL-managed accounts and as a standalone product.
tools.real_estate_use: Its distinguishing feature in daily use is vendor scoring: response and completion performance is measured per provider, so dispatch can route to the contractor who actually shows up rather than the one with the oldest relationship. For an occupier outsourcing facilities management, it also gives visibility into work the service provider is performing on their behalf.
features: Service request intake and automated vendor dispatch
Vendor performance scoring and compliance tracking
Preventive maintenance scheduling
Asset registry with repair-versus-replace history
Invoice and spend controls per work order
Portfolio dashboards for occupancy cost and service levels

use_cases.job: Route work to the contractors with the best measured completion performance
See what an outsourced facilities provider is actually doing across the portfolio

tools.name: HappyCo
tools.positioning: Maintenance and asset-condition platform for multifamily operators, built around mobile inspections, work orders and unit turns.
tools.description: HappyCo is an operations platform for multifamily owners and property managers organized into several suites: maintenance operations (preventive maintenance, work orders, make-readies, inspections and reporting), an after-hours answering and triage service that turns resident calls into work orders, asset management covering capital budgets, renovation projects, vendor compliance and inventory, asset evaluation for due diligence and lease-file audits, and a sourcing module for vendor bidding. Its mobile apps work offline and sync when connectivity returns, and it integrates with the main property management systems as a certified partner. A separate lending suite connects to Freddie Mac's Optigo network for origination inspections.
tools.real_estate_use: A regional manager responsible for several thousand apartments cannot personally see the condition of any of them. Their onsite technicians run every inspection — move-in, move-out, life safety, make-ready — inside the HappyCo mobile app, which timestamps photos and pushes the result back with no paper. When a unit is vacated, the make-ready workflow assigns the punch list and the manager watches the turn close in a dashboard rather than by phone. At acquisition, the same apps are used for due-diligence walks and lease-file audits so the buyer's condition assessment sits in the system the operator will use afterwards. Overnight resident calls are triaged by the answering service and arrive the next morning as work orders already routed.
features: Mobile inspections with timestamped photos and offline sync
Work orders, preventive maintenance schedules and make-ready turn tracking
After-hours call triage that generates work orders automatically
Capital budget, renovation project and vendor compliance tracking
Due-diligence and lease-file audit workflows for acquisitions
Benchmarking dashboards across properties, units and staff

use_cases.job: Run move-in, move-out and life-safety inspections on mobile and close a unit turn against a tracked punch list
Schedule preventive maintenance and dispatch work orders to onsite technicians across a portfolio
Carry out due-diligence walks and lease-file audits on an acquisition inside the platform the operator will keep using

integrations: Certified integrations with leading property management systems

tools.name: Hemlane
tools.positioning: Software plus a local agent and a 24/7 repair desk — for the owner who is not in the same city as the property.
tools.description: Hemlane combines rental management software with optional human services: a local leasing agent network for showings, and 24/7 maintenance coordination that triages tenant calls and dispatches vendors. Owners choose how much of the operation to delegate.
tools.real_estate_use: It targets the remote owner who does not want a full management company taking eight to ten percent. The software handles marketing, screening and rent; the local agent handles the showing that cannot be done remotely; the repair desk answers the two a.m. burst pipe. The economics sit deliberately between self-management and full delegation.
features: Listing syndication and applicant screening
Local leasing agent network for showings
24/7 maintenance coordination and vendor dispatch
Rent collection with automated reminders
Lease tracking with state-specific compliance guidance
Owner reporting and financial exports

use_cases.job: Manage an out-of-state rental without paying full management fees
Have someone answer the emergency maintenance call at night

tools.name: Limble CMMS
tools.positioning: The CMMS bought because the last CMMS was never adopted.
tools.description: Limble is a maintenance management system covering work orders, preventive maintenance, asset management, parts inventory and reporting, sold heavily on ease of configuration and speed of rollout, with published pricing and a self-serve trial.
tools.real_estate_use: Most CMMS failures are adoption failures, not feature gaps. Limble competes on the implementation: QR codes on equipment so a technician scans rather than searches, a request portal that needs no login for the person reporting a problem, and configuration a facilities lead can do without consultants.
features: QR code asset tagging for scan-to-report and scan-to-log
Work order management with automated assignment
Preventive maintenance by time, usage or condition
Parts inventory with automatic reordering
No-login request portal for occupants
Custom dashboards and maintenance KPI reporting

use_cases.job: Roll out a maintenance system that technicians actually use within weeks
Report a building problem by scanning a code without an account

tools.name: Matterport
tools.positioning: The 3D capture standard — a walkable digital twin that doubles as a measurable record of the space.
tools.description: Matterport captures buildings in 3D using dedicated cameras or a phone, producing walkable virtual tours, automatic floor plans, measurements and structured space data hosted on its cloud platform, embeddable in listings and other systems.
tools.real_estate_use: In marketing, a scan lets a remote buyer or tenant walk the space before travelling. In operations it does something less obvious and often more valuable: it is a dated, measurable record of condition. Property managers scan at move-in and move-out to settle deposit disputes; facility teams scan plant rooms so a contractor can measure without a site visit.
features: 3D capture from dedicated cameras or smartphone
Walkable virtual tours embeddable in listings
Automatic floor plan and measurement generation
Dated condition records for inspections and disputes
Space and asset tagging inside the model
API and integrations with listing and management platforms

use_cases.job: Let a remote buyer or tenant walk the property before travelling to see it
Hold a dated, measurable condition record for move-in and move-out disputes

tools.name: MRI Software
tools.positioning: The open alternative to a single-vendor stack — bring your own best-of-breed and let MRI hold the lease and the ledger.
tools.description: MRI Software provides property and lease management, accounting, investment management, facilities and workplace products across commercial and residential real estate worldwide. Its stated strategy is an open platform: published APIs and a partner ecosystem rather than a closed suite.
tools.real_estate_use: A European or transatlantic owner often cannot standardise on one vendor — local accounting, local leasing practice and existing systems all resist it. MRI is chosen when the lease and financial core must be common while country teams keep their own tools around it. In France it supports local lease and accounting requirements alongside Anglo-Saxon reporting.
features: Commercial and residential lease and property management
Real estate accounting with multi-entity and multi-currency
Investment management and investor reporting
Facilities management and workplace modules
Lease accounting compliance for IFRS 16 and ASC 842
Open APIs and a partner integration ecosystem

use_cases.job: Consolidate a cross-border portfolio while local teams keep their own tools
Meet IFRS 16 lease accounting obligations from the lease system itself

tools.name: Property Meld
tools.positioning: Residential maintenance coordination as its own discipline — because it is where property managers lose their margin and their reputation.
tools.description: Property Meld handles the maintenance workflow for residential property management: tenant request intake with triage, vendor scheduling and coordination, communication across all parties, and analytics on speed and cost per repair.
tools.real_estate_use: In residential management, maintenance is the largest source of complaints and the biggest drain on staff time — mostly spent as phone tag between a tenant, a vendor and an owner trying to agree a time. Property Meld automates the scheduling coordination, and its metrics — median speed to resolution, cost per unit — are the ones managers now report to owners.
features: Tenant maintenance request intake with guided triage
Automated vendor and tenant scheduling coordination
Owner approval workflows for repairs above a threshold
Vendor performance and cost analytics
Communication log across tenant, vendor and owner
Speed-to-resolution and cost-per-unit reporting

use_cases.job: Eliminate phone tag between tenant, vendor and owner on every repair
Approve repairs above a threshold with the evidence in front of you

tools.name: RentCheck
tools.positioning: Tenant-guided property inspections: the resident completes the inspection from their phone, the manager gets the report.
tools.description: RentCheck is an inspection application for residential property managers built around inspections carried out by the tenant rather than by staff. The manager sends a guided inspection; the resident completes it step by step on their phone with time-stamped photos, and a report is produced without a site visit. It ships with templates for move-in, move-out and routine inspections, automated reminders and scheduling, comparison against previous inspections, work order tracking, an API and integrations with the main property management systems. Pricing is published per unit per month.
tools.real_estate_use: A property management company adding doors hits a wall on inspections: scheduling visits, chasing tenants for access and driving between properties does not scale, so routine inspections quietly get skipped for the tenants presumed to be fine. RentCheck inverts the model — the tenant does the walkthrough on their phone with a guided checklist and timestamped photos — so the team handles only the exceptions. The photographic record with dates is also what settles a security deposit dispute at move-out, since move-in and move-out inspections can be compared side by side.
features: Tenant-guided inspections with time-stamped in-app photo capture
Templates for move-in, move-out, routine and pre-move-out inspections
Automated inspection reminders and scheduling
Comparison against previous inspections
360-degree photo and video capture, and asset capture
Work order tracking, PMS integration and a public API

use_cases.job: Complete routine inspections across a growing portfolio without sending anyone on site
Hold a dated photographic record of condition at move-in to settle the deposit at move-out

tools.name: Rent Manager
tools.positioning: The configurable one — for portfolios whose lease terms do not fit anybody's standard form.
tools.description: Rent Manager is a property management and accounting platform known for the depth of its configuration: user-defined fields, custom reports, a built-in contact centre, work order and asset tracking, and support for unusual property types including self-storage, marinas, manufactured housing and mixed portfolios.
tools.real_estate_use: It wins where the standard product breaks. A portfolio mixing apartments, commercial suites, storage units and ground leases has billing rules no template covers; Rent Manager lets an operator model them without leaving the accounting system. The trade-off is that someone has to own the configuration.
features: Configurable accounting with user-defined fields and custom reports
Support for storage, marina, manufactured housing and mixed portfolios
Work order, inspection and fixed-asset tracking
Built-in phone system and contact centre
Tenant and owner portals with online payments
Open API and extensive integration marketplace

use_cases.job: Model non-standard billing across a mixed-asset portfolio inside the accounting system
Track work orders and equipment against the same property records as the leases

tools.name: ServiceChannel
tools.positioning: Facilities management for multi-site occupiers — one contractor marketplace, one invoice standard, across hundreds of locations.
tools.description: ServiceChannel manages facilities maintenance for multi-location businesses: work order dispatch, a contractor network with compliance tracking, invoice validation against agreed rates, asset and warranty tracking, and spend analytics across sites.
tools.real_estate_use: A retailer with four hundred stores has four hundred sets of local contractors and no consistent way to know whether a bill is fair. ServiceChannel standardises the workflow: a store manager raises an issue, dispatch goes to a compliant contractor at contracted rates, and invoices that exceed the agreed rate are flagged before payment. The saving is in the invoice validation as much as in the dispatch.
features: Work order intake, dispatch and tracking across sites
Contractor network with insurance and compliance verification
Invoice validation against contracted rates
Asset and warranty tracking by location
Planned maintenance scheduling
Spend analytics by site, trade and provider

use_cases.job: Standardise maintenance dispatch and invoice control across hundreds of sites
See maintenance spend by trade and location instead of by supplier invoice

tools.name: SpinalCom
tools.positioning: A building operating system — the layer that makes twenty proprietary building systems queryable as one digital twin.
tools.description: SpinalCom publishes a building operating system that aggregates data from heterogeneous building systems — HVAC, lighting, access, metering, BIM models — into a semantic digital twin, exposed through APIs so applications can be built on top rather than integrated one by one.
tools.real_estate_use: A smart building project usually stalls on the same wall: every subsystem speaks a different protocol and belongs to a different contractor. Placing an operating system between the equipment and the applications means the tenant app, the energy dashboard and the maintenance tool all read the same model of the building, and replacing a supplier does not break everything above it.
features: Aggregation of heterogeneous building systems and protocols
Semantic digital twin linked to the BIM model
Open APIs for third-party applications
Real-time supervision and equipment monitoring
Data historisation for energy and operations analytics
Vendor-independent architecture

use_cases.job: Read every building subsystem through one model instead of twenty interfaces
Build tenant and energy applications on a twin that outlives a supplier change

tools.name: Twimm
tools.positioning: A French CMMS written for the maintenance company as much as for the building owner.
tools.description: Twimm is a French SaaS platform for technical building maintenance: contract and site management, preventive and corrective intervention planning, technician mobile app with on-site reports, spare parts, quotes and invoicing tied to the intervention.
tools.real_estate_use: In France the maintenance of a building is usually outsourced under a contract with defined preventive obligations. Twimm holds both sides: the contractual preventive plan and the corrective calls, with the technician's signed report as the evidence of execution. That evidence is what a manager needs when a landlord asks whether the contract was actually performed.
features: Maintenance contract and site management
Preventive plan scheduling from contractual obligations
Corrective intervention dispatch and tracking
Technician mobile app with on-site signed reports
Quotes, spare parts and invoicing per intervention
Regulatory inspection follow-up

use_cases.job: Prove that contractual preventive maintenance was actually carried out
Track corrective interventions across a portfolio with signed field reports

tools.name: UpKeep
tools.positioning: A CMMS designed for the technician's phone first, so work actually gets logged.
tools.description: UpKeep is a mobile-first maintenance management platform: work orders, preventive maintenance schedules, asset records, parts inventory and reporting, with the technician experience as the primary design surface rather than the manager's dashboard.
tools.real_estate_use: Maintenance data quality fails at the point of capture — a technician who has to return to a desktop to close a ticket will close five at once from memory on Friday. Building it for the phone, with photos and offline capture, is what makes the asset history usable a year later when deciding whether to repair or replace a rooftop unit.
features: Mobile work order creation, assignment and completion
Preventive maintenance schedules by asset or meter reading
Asset registry with full repair history
Parts and inventory tracking with reorder alerts
Request portal for occupants and staff
Downtime, cost and technician performance reporting

use_cases.job: Get technicians to log work at the point of work rather than from memory
Build an equipment repair history that justifies a capital replacement

tools.name: Wattsense
tools.positioning: Plug-in connectivity for buildings too small to justify a full BMS integration project.
tools.description: Wattsense provides a hardware and cloud solution that connects a building's existing equipment — boilers, HVAC, meters, controllers — across multiple protocols and exposes the data and control points through a single cloud API, without a bespoke integration project.
tools.real_estate_use: Most of a commercial portfolio is not headquarters buildings. Mid-sized assets have some automation, no standardisation, and no budget for a systems integrator per site. Wattsense targets exactly that middle: a box on site, protocols handled, data and control available remotely — which is what makes portfolio-wide energy management feasible below the flagship tier.
features: Multi-protocol connectivity to existing building equipment
Cloud API for data collection and remote control
Deployment without a bespoke integration project
Remote monitoring and alerting across sites
Data normalisation across heterogeneous equipment
Partner integrations with energy and facility platforms

use_cases.job: Connect mid-sized buildings to remote monitoring without an integration project each
Standardise data collection across a portfolio of heterogeneous equipment

tools.name: Yuman
tools.positioning: A modern French CMMS built mobile-first for technicians in the field.
tools.description: Yuman is a French maintenance management SaaS covering equipment records, preventive maintenance plans, work orders, technician scheduling and route planning, mobile field reporting, spare parts, quotes and invoicing.
tools.real_estate_use: Its buyers are maintenance companies and technical services teams working across many sites, where the daily constraint is routing technicians efficiently and capturing what they did. The field application works offline in plant rooms and basements — a mundane requirement that decides whether the data exists at all.
features: Equipment and site registry with maintenance history
Preventive maintenance plans and automatic work order generation
Technician scheduling with route optimisation
Offline-capable mobile field reporting
Spare parts and stock management
Quotes, invoicing and contract profitability tracking

use_cases.job: Schedule and route technicians across many sites and capture work offline
Keep a per-equipment maintenance history that supports replacement decisions
